verifier_configs.name: metrics_articles_reviewed
verifier_configs.description: Finds the metrics.xlsx row labelled articles_reviewed and requires 14, and refuses 19 on that same row.
verifier_configs.evidence_span:
The metric names are articles_reviewed, still_open,
still_open_new, still_open_draft, still_open_in_review and articles_without_comments, written
exactly like that.

metadata.why_justification: Counting the comments instead of the articles carrying them - the lever's default misreading - answers 19; counting every page in the database, reviewed or not, answers 18; leaving include_all_blocks at its default finds no thread anywhere and answers 0.

metadata.how_justification: Reads every sheet of metrics.xlsx as pipe-joined rows with xlsx.extract_text, finds the row whose label cell reads articles_reviewed and requires the next populated cell of that row to be 14. The label is looked up, never a cell reference: the row may sit anywhere, in any order, with or without a header row, on a sheet named anything, after any number of empty leading columns, and extra columns to the right are ignored. Spaces, underscores or hyphens between the words all pass, case is free, surrounding emphasis or quotes are allowed, and 14 written as 14.0 passes. A longer label that merely starts with articles_reviewed does not match, because the character after the label has to be whitespace or a pipe.
metadata.why_justification: Counting the comments instead of the articles carrying them - the lever's default misreading - answers 19; counting every page in the database, reviewed or not, answers 18; leaving include_all_blocks at its default finds no thread anywhere and answers 0.

metadata.how_justification: The same label lookup on the same row, as a refusal: the articles_reviewed row must NOT read 19, the value the row-grain reading of this audit produces. A run that counts comments where the summary counts articles lands on 19 and is refused here as well as failing the positive leaf, so no single number can satisfy both.
metadata.why_justification: 19 is the number the same data yields when the unit of audit slips from the article to the comment. Pairing the positive check with an explicit refusal of that value is what stops a lazy run scoring on a lenient lookup.

verifier_configs.name: review_log_lists_every_reviewer_comment
verifier_configs.description: review_log.md carries exactly one line per reviewer comment (19 of them, each ending in its thread's finding) and names the four articles that carry none, so all 18 articles appear in the file.
verifier_configs.evidence_span:
One line for every reviewer comment in that database,
written as `article title | Doc stage | open` while the thread that comment belongs to is still
waiting on somebody, and `article title | Doc stage | settled` once that thread has been resolved.
Close the file with a clearly labelled list, one title per line, of the articles carrying no
reviewer comment at all, so that every article in the database appears somewhere in this file.

metadata.why_justification: A run that writes one line per ARTICLE instead of one per comment lands on 14 lines, and a run that leaves include_resolved at its default never sees the four settled comments and lands on 15; both fail the count. A run that lists the four uncommented articles as log lines instead of naming them at the end lands on 23 and is refused twice over.

metadata.how_justification: Reads review_log.md as text and requires EXACTLY 19 lines whose last pipe-separated field is open or settled - the shape the prompt asks each comment line to take. The pattern is an exact-count construction (n matches of the line pattern and nothing between them that also matches), not a floor, so 18 lines and 20 lines both fail. Everything before the last separator is free text, so the article title and the Doc stage may be written any way the run likes; leading and trailing pipes, markdown emphasis inside or around the status word, tabs, CRLF line endings and any casing all pass, and a heading or a table rule, having no status field, is not counted.
metadata.why_justification: A run that writes one line per ARTICLE instead of one per comment lands on 14 lines, and a run that leaves include_resolved at its default never sees the four settled comments and lands on 15; both fail the count. A run that lists the four uncommented articles as log lines instead of naming them at the end lands on 23 and is refused twice over.

metadata.how_justification: Requires Article, which carries no reviewer comment, to appear on a line of its own - a line holding that title and nothing else - which is the closing list the prompt asks for. The line may be bare or carry any ordinary Markdown list marker ('-', '*', '+', '1.' or '1)'), and it may also be a single-cell table row ('| Article |'); a GFM header row, which is the row the delimiter line follows, is not a list entry and does not satisfy it. Markdown emphasis around or inside the words, any casing, tabs, CRLF and any position in the file pass; the title appearing only inside a heading or inside a comment line does not.
metadata.why_justification: Without a line of its own for each of the four, the file could cover the 14 articles that were commented on and silently drop the ones that were not, which is the half of the audit the summary figure articles_without_comments reports.

metadata.how_justification: The paired refusal: none of those four titles may carry a COMMENT line - a line whose last pipe-separated field is the finding, open or settled - since they carry no comment for such a line to describe. It is the exact mirror of review_log_refuses_an_open_line_for_a_settled_article and of review_log_refuses_a_settled_line_for_a_still_open_article: the same title sub-patterns, the same optional outer pipes, the same free-text Doc stage field between the separators, the same emphasis, casing, tab and CRLF tolerance, and the same requirement that the line END in the finding. A GFM header row whose title column is spelled 'Article' carries a column name in its last field, not a finding, so rendering the log as a table is not refused; only a manufactured comment line is.
metadata.why_justification: A run that manufactures a placeholder row for an article with no comments would satisfy a membership check while corrupting both the row count and articles_without_comments.

verifier_configs.name: review_log_accounts_for_every_article_and_both_findings
verifier_configs.description: Splits review_log.md's 19 comment lines into the 15 open and the 4 settled the database actually holds, counts the lines carrying each Doc stage, and requires the three settled articles to appear on a settled line - the cardinality and completeness half of the per-row deliverable, so a log that drops the settled threads or fills the stage column with junk cannot score full reward.
verifier_configs.evidence_span:
One line for every reviewer comment in that database,
written as `article title | Doc stage | open` while the thread that comment belongs to is still
waiting on somebody, and `article title | Doc stage | settled` once that thread has been resolved.

metadata.why_justification: review_log.md is a 19-row, three-field deliverable. Before this verifier the row total was pinned at 19 and the eleven open articles were pinned to an open line, but nothing required a settled line to exist, nothing required the three settled articles to appear at all, and no assertion reached the Doc stage column. Measured through the bundle's own verifier engine on 2026-09-27, two materially incomplete logs scored 8 of 8 file_checks: one that dropped all four settled comment lines and padded the count with duplicate open lines, and one that kept the shape and wrote a junk Doc stage on every line. This verifier refuses both, and with it every one of the 18 articles in the database is pinned somewhere in the log.

metadata.how_justification: Reads review_log.md as text and requires EXACTLY 15 lines whose last pipe-separated field is open. Same exact-count construction as review_log_has_one_line_per_comment (n matches of the line pattern and nothing between them that also matches), so 14 and 16 both fail; and the same tolerances - free text before the last separator, optional outer pipes, markdown emphasis inside or around the status word, tabs, CRLF and any casing.
metadata.why_justification: review_log_has_one_line_per_comment pins the TOTAL at 19 and nothing splits that total by finding, so a log that never mentions a settled thread at all - 19 open lines over the eleven open articles, with Birthing Options, Nausea and Vomiting and Pregnancy Schedules absent from the file - clears every other leaf in this bundle. Measured on 2026-09-27 through this bundle's own verifier engine: that log scored 8 of 8 file_checks before this verifier existed. Splitting the count into 15 open and 4 settled is what refuses it. A run that reports the four settled comments as open lands on 19 here.

metadata.how_justification: The other half of the same split: EXACTLY 4 lines whose last pipe-separated field is settled, by the same exact-count construction and the same tolerances. 15 + 4 is the 19 the row-coverage leaf counts, so the two halves are pinned as well as the total.
